pipeline_name: Kodr.pro High-Assurance Contract Verification & Security Pipeline
execution_model: Fail-Closed Gated Pipeline with Dual-Cadence Tiers, Binary Gate Verdicts, and Expert-in-the-Loop Attestation
official_description: Kodr.pro High-Assurance Contract Verification & Security Pipeline (v0.1.0) is a fail-closed, dual-cadence verification system for EVM smart contracts. It enforces hermetic, fully pinned builds (Docker digest-pinned toolchain) and runs every stage under a binary GO/NO-GO gate. On every pull request it performs supply-chain and SBOM checks, deterministic compilation with bytecode size limits, static analysis with governed suppressions, event-emission and indexing verification, storage-layout and upgrade-safety analysis (including Diamond/ERC-2535), ERC standard conformance, and unit, differential, and mainnet-fork testing at >=95% coverage. On the release gate it adds an exhaustive access-control matrix, mutation testing (>=90% kill rate), multi-engine stateful fuzzing with cross-contract reentrancy handlers, source- and bytecode-level symbolic execution with dual bounded model checking (solc SMTChecker and hevm), EVM-level formal theorem proving via Kontrol (KEVM/K Framework) whose non-vacuity check is a written per-proof rationale rather than a coverage metric (Kontrol 1.0.255 reports none), and a signed expert threat-model and specification review. The final stage cryptographically attests the entire evidence bundle.
capabilities: Reproducible builds, dependency hygiene, comprehensive static and dynamic analysis, formal verification of specified properties (bounded model checking and EVM-level theorem proving), upgrade and access-control safety, standards compliance, and cryptographically signed provenance.
security_level: Among the strongest practical pre-deployment assurance processes currently achievable with open tooling. It provides high confidence that the code matches its stated invariants, access controls, and specifications, subject to the completeness of those specifications and the quality of the expert review. It does not eliminate residual risk from incomplete threat models or novel economic attacks.

toolchain_environment.hermetic_runtime: Pinned Docker image digests. All stages execute inside containers whose base images and tool artifacts are digest/sha256-pinned in docker/pins.env; hacvsp doctor verifies every pin fail-closed before any stage is permitted to run.

aiwrangler_mcp.runtime: MCP server (@kodr/aiwrangler), invoked by the pipeline agent over the Model Context Protocol; not a CLI. Used for AST diff triage, gate verification assistance, and human-review acknowledgement of suppression-ratification findings.

stages.objective: Audit external dependencies, generate CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM, enforce cryptographic tag verification, and freeze immutable git submodules.

software.name: Syft / Trivy
software.purpose: Generate and scan CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM for smart contract submodules, npm packages, and compiler binaries.

software.name: cargo-audit / npm audit / git
software.purpose: Enforce exact commit-pinned git submodules or locked package digests (reject floating SemVer).

requirements.dependency_policy: All external dependencies must be pinned to explicit release commit hashes with verified cryptographic tags; zero untracked dependencies.

gate.criteria: Zero unreviewed CVEs in third-party libraries; all submodules pinned to immutable commit hashes.

stages.objective: Produce byte-for-byte reproducible build artifacts, lock compiler flags, and validate EVM runtime bytecode and initcode boundaries.

gate.criteria: Bytecode matches bit-for-bit in clean hermetic container; zero contracts violate EIP-170 or EIP-3860 size boundaries.

stages.objective: Execute static analysis, detect unbounded loops/gas griefing, parse specification annotations, and enforce suppression governance.

software.name: Scribble
software.purpose: Parse and validate inline specification annotations (invariants, pre/post conditions, ghost variables).

software.name: SARIF Aggregator
software.purpose: Normalize findings and enforce strict suppression gating against .security-suppressions.json.

analysis_targets: Unbounded loops and external-call DoS vectors
Unprotected state changes and reentrancy paths
requirements.suppression_policy: Every suppressed finding must specify finding_id, file, line_range, git_commit_hash, justification, and reviewer_signature in .security-suppressions.json.

gate.criteria: Zero unsuppressed static warnings; 100% of suppression entries cryptographically signed and structurally valid.

stages.objective: Verify that all critical state mutations emit strongly typed events with appropriate indexed topics for monitoring, subgraphs, and incident triage.

software.name: AiWrangler MCP
software.runtime: MCP server (@kodr/aiwrangler 0.1.5), driven by the pipeline agent over MCP; not a CLI
software.purpose: Triage AST state diffs and the extracted mutation graph, and acknowledge any human-severity findings raised during event-emission verification.

software.name: Event Audit Engine
software.runtime: Custom stdlib-Python tool (tools/event-audit) over foundry build-info ASTs
software.purpose: Extract the state-mutation graph from the canonical AST and verify a matching event emission for every critical mutation.

software.name: Slither
software.purpose: Flag any public or external state-modifying function that updates storage variables without emitting a matching event.

rules: Every state variable mutation involving ownership, fee parameters, access rights, pause states, balances, or core protocol parameters must emit a dedicated event.
Indexed fields must include actor/caller address and target/asset identifiers (max 3 indexed topics per event per EVM specification).
Reentrancy guards and state updates must precede or immediately accompany event emission.

gate.criteria: Zero missing events on state-modifying functions; all primary entity identifiers correctly indexed.

stages.objective: Verify storage slot preservation, proxy initialization safety, storage gaps, and Diamond (ERC-2535) facet/selector integrity.

software.name: OpenZeppelin Upgrades CLI / Foundry plugin
software.purpose: Verify classic proxy storage layout preservation against baseline commits.

software.name: Foundry
software.purpose: Extract concrete storage slots, types, and offsets.

software.name: Layout Diff Engine
software.purpose: Verify storage layout preservation against the baseline commit, storage gap arithmetic, Diamond storage namespace immutability, and absence of four-byte selector collisions across registered facets.

checks: Zero alteration to slot assignment or types of pre-existing storage variables across updates
Storage gap integrity verified (__gap array size decreases strictly equal to added variables)
Constructors lock implementation logic (_disableInitializers() or equivalent in logic constructor)
Diamond storage namespace hashes collision-free and immutable
No four-byte function selector collisions across registered Diamond facets

gate.criteria: Zero storage collision warnings; formal confirmation of initializer protection and facet selector uniqueness.

stages.objective: Verify strict conformance to standard interface specifications and mathematical boundary constraints.

software.name: Foundry ERC Conformance Harness
software.purpose: Validate ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155, and ERC-4626 conformance against canonical test suites.

software.name: ERC-4626 Property Test Suite (a16z / OpenZeppelin)
software.purpose: Prove share-to-asset accounting rounding directions (round down on mint/deposit, round up on withdraw/redeem to protect pool solvency).

conformance_specs: EIP-4626 mathematical inflation attack immunity / slippage tolerances

gate.criteria: 100% pass across all applicable reference standard compliance suites.

stages.objective: Validate concrete state transitions, differential math against reference implementations, gas limits, and real mainnet-fork environments.

software.name: Differential Test Engine
software.purpose: Execute side-by-side differential tests comparing contract state and math calculations against known-good reference implementations (e.g., Solady, OpenZeppelin, or canonical Python/Rust models).

software.name: Anvil
software.purpose: Local mainnet/testnet fork execution simulating live DEX liquidity, oracle staleness, and lending interactions.

coverage_thresholds.exceptions_policy: Any branch under 100% requires a documented justification in COVERAGE_EXCEPTIONS.md (e.g., unreachable compiler artifacts or defensive panic catches).

differential_testing_scope: Math routines tested against reference math models across bounded input spaces
Token logic tested against standard reference implementations to detect state divergence
fork_testing_scope: External oracle latency and stale data simulation
Flash loan callback interaction under real pool states
Liquidity depth constraints and price impact limits

gate.criteria: All unit, differential, and fork tests pass; coverage meets >= 95% threshold with all gap justifications approved.

stages.objective: Generate and mathematically enforce an exhaustive Access Control Matrix mapping roles to external/public state transitions.

software.name: Access Matrix Extractor
software.purpose: Extract all public/external entry points and their associated modifiers/guards into a structured graph.

software.name: Access Matrix Assertion Engine
software.runtime: Foundry test harness (generated from the matrix)
software.purpose: Systematically exercise entry points using non-privileged addresses to prove authorization bounds and enforce 100% concordance between the declared matrix and executable tests.

gate.criteria: Zero unauthorized callers can execute privileged state-modifying functions; 100% concordance between declared matrix and executable tests.

stages.objective: Measure test suite assertion quality by injecting semantic mutations into the codebase and calculating kill rates.

software.name: Gambit
software.purpose: Generate syntactic and semantic mutations (inverted booleans, altered math operators, bypassed requirements).

software.name: Foundry Runner
software.purpose: Execute the test harness against each injected mutant to verify detection; compute kill rate and triage survivors.

requirements.mutation_score_threshold: >= 90% mutant kill rate across audited core contracts.
requirements.triage: Every surviving mutant must be analyzed: either patch the test harness with the missing assertion or document mutant equivalence in MUTATION_EXCEPTIONS.md.

gate.criteria: Mutation kill rate meets or exceeds 90%; zero unaddressed live mutants in core accounting logic.

stages.objective: Attempt to violate global system invariants across high-depth pseudo-random call sequences and cross-contract callback chains.

handler_architecture: Actor ghost accounts simulating non-privileged users vs. admin addresses
Cross-contract reentrancy-set handlers simulating malicious token and receiver hooks
invariant_domains: Conservation of capital (Total assets == total liabilities + protocol equity)
Solvency invariants across extreme multi-call combinations
Strict access control invariants (unprivileged callers cannot alter critical parameters)

gate.criteria: Zero invariant violations after target runs and depth across all active fuzzing engines.

stages.objective: Explore symbolic execution pathways at both source level and compiled EVM bytecode level, with dual bounded model checking engines.

software.name: hevm (argotorg fork)
software.purpose: Symbolic execution of Foundry tests: proves test_Proof_* properties for all symbolic inputs. Replaces halmos (dormant since 2025-08, incompatible with forge-1.9 build-info).

software.name: Mythril
software.purpose: Bytecode-level taint analysis, path exploration, and detection of delegatecall/unprotected selfdestruct vulnerabilities independent of Solidity AST quirks.

analysis_targets: Absence of arithmetic overflows/underflows in low-level assembly / unchecked blocks
Bytecode taint analysis confirming sensitive storage slots cannot be overwritten by arbitrary call inputs

gate.criteria: All bounded paths proven safe; zero unmitigated bytecode vulnerabilities reported by Mythril/hevm.

stages.objective: Formally prove matched Foundry tests at the EVM bytecode level with Kontrol (KEVM). Pinned Kontrol 1.0.255 has no proof-coverage metric; non-vacuity is a written rationale in review/KONTROL_VACUITY.md.

software.name: Kontrol (Runtime Verification)
software.runtime: Pinned Docker digest (KEVM / K Framework), image tag 1.0.255
software.purpose: Compile the matched Foundry tests to KEVM and prove them at the bytecode level. This version has no coverage subcommand; kontrol list is an inventory only.

spec_verification: Matched Foundry tests (default match Proof*) are proved with kontrol prove. The gate fails if no proof ran or any proof failed
Kontrol 1.0.255 writes no coverage percentage. The runner stores coverage_pct as null. kontrol_coverage_min_pct is recorded and not applied

review/KONTROL_VACUITY.md must exist, contain the text 'coverage: tool-unavailable', and include every name in kontrol-proofs.json passed and failed. Those names are the --match-test patterns, not a parsed list of test functions. The gate does not verify a signature on that file
Stage 11 hevm proves Foundry tests prefixed test_Proof under test/proofs/. Stage 12 does not re-check that result. Stage 13 signs MANUAL_REVIEW_SIGNOFF.md, not the vacuity file

gate.criteria: Zero failed Kontrol proofs and at least one proof ran. review/KONTROL_VACUITY.md exists, names every recorded proof, and states that coverage is tool-unavailable. No coverage threshold is applied. The gate does not check a signature on that file.

stages.objective: Synthesize automated results, execute adversarial manual review, conduct economic/MEV attack analysis, audit specifications, and ratify all active suppressions.

responsibilities: Specification correctness and completeness audit against protocol whitepaper
Privilege and governance escalation pathway mapping against ACCESS_CONTROL_MATRIX.json
Economic attack, oracle manipulation, and MEV extraction analysis
Cross-contract reentrancy and composability risk review
Final verification and sign-off on all entries within .security-suppressions.json and COVERAGE_EXCEPTIONS.md

participants.runtime: LLM via isolated API / local sandbox (separate OpenCode agent session)
responsibilities: Adversarial diff analysis between git commits
Semantic checklist verification of business logic against protocol whitepaper
Second-pair-of-eyes check on proof-spec completeness (hevm/Kontrol corpus) and test edge cases

review_deliverables: THREAT_MODEL.md (Actor matrix, trust boundaries, economic vectors, MEV exposure)
SPEC_AUDIT.md (Confirmation that written invariants match actual business intent)
MANUAL_REVIEW_SIGNOFF.md (Explicit review log of high-risk assembly, internal accounting functions, and active suppression audit)

gate.criteria: Signed cryptographic approval by Principal Security Engineer certifying threat model coverage, invariant completeness, and suppression justifications.

stages.objective: Generate immutable provenance receipts, sign test and analysis digests, compile the active suppression inventory, and publish the verified assurance bundle.

software.name: Cosign / Sigstore
software.purpose: Keyless or keyed cryptographic signing of all test receipts, build manifests, and SBOMs.

software.name: GitHub Actions / Attestation
software.purpose: Generate SLSA-compliant in-toto provenance attestations bound to the specific commit SHA.

software.name: Sourcify & Explorer CLI
software.purpose: Exact match bytecode verification on block explorers with matching metadata IPFS hash.

software.name: Attestation Engine
software.purpose: Hash and assemble the evidence bundle, render SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md, drive cosign signing, and verify the signed bundle.

mandatory_sections: Active Suppressions & Exceptions Inventory (Table: Tool, Rule ID, Target File/Line, Justification, Authorizing Reviewer, Commit SHA)

gate.criteria: All signed attestations, verifiable build hashes, active suppression tables, and execution logs committed to public repository root.
